modules.name: Layer 0 data model and open-schema mapping
modules.design_question: What minimum geometry-plus-program record lets every module read one design consistently, including storeys, podium, public realm and access points, and export it to IFC, Speckle, glTF and BOT?
modules.effort: M: core schema v0 with FloorPlate, JSON and GLB-with-extras export about 3 person-days; IFC4 exporter about 2, BOT mapper 1 and Speckle 2026.9 mapper 2 more in v1 (team estimate)
inputs: Imported or modelled geometry (meshes, B-reps, extrusions)
User program tags (office, residential, hotel, retail, cultural/civic, public, amenity, mechanical, core)
Site boundary polygon, street frontage lines, access points and viewpoints (drawn by the user or supplied by P14-M08)
Storey schedule and FloorPlate records written by P14-M04
Georeference record from P14-M03: CRS, Z0 geodetic elevation, vertical datum, north type, true north
outputs: Layer0 JSON (Z-up, right-handed, metres) with typed ports: Site, Podium, Tower, Level (negative elevations below grade), ProgramVolume, FloorPlate, OpenSpace, Frontage, AccessPoint, Viewpoint, ViewCone, ContextBuilding, Assumption
Per-level, per-tag area table: gross_area, counted_fsr_area, counts_to_employment_FSR, fsr_exclusion_reason
Mapping table: each class to its IFC, Speckle, glTF and BOT target with status mapped, custom property set or missing
GLB with node extras (core); IFC4 ADD2 export (IfcSite > IfcBuilding > IfcBuildingStorey > IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone), BOT Turtle graph and Speckle 2026.9 version (v1)
Result-card provenance fields (source_id, snapshot hash)

parameters.name: Spatial hierarchy and shared podium
parameters.relationship: Site > Building > Storey > Space maps one-to-one in IFC and BOT. IFC links each storey to a single building, so a shared podium becomes its own building under the towers (to confirm). Finer records enable per-floor metrics but raise tagging effort.

parameters.name: Storey slicing of volumes into FloorPlates
parameters.relationship: A massing volume spans many floors but an IfcSpace sits in one storey. Slicing each volume on the storey schedule gives per-floor area for the FSR check, core ratio and daylight; the volume maps to an IfcSpatialZone grouping its plates.

parameters.name: Program vocabulary (9 tags)
parameters.relationship: More tags give a finer use split but each needs a classification entry; fewer tags reduce disagreement. Tags must roll up to the brief's use groups and travel as IfcClassificationReference, which IFC tools can read, not only as a custom property.

parameters.name: FSR-counted area definition (gross vs counted, employment flag per tag)
parameters.relationship: The brief's 9.0 FSR minimum of non-residential, high-employment area (about 103,200 m2 on 11,468 m2, derived) depends on what counts. Gross versus counted area, exclusions (mechanical, below grade, amenity) and the per-tag flag change the shortfall; by-law wording is unread.

parameters.name: Geometry carrier (display mesh vs exact B-rep)
parameters.relationship: Triangle meshes approximate curved faces, so area and volume error grows with tessellation tolerance; exact B-rep keeps volume but is heavy in a browser. Speckle's earlier object graph likewise separated display meshes from source objects.

parameters.name: Z origin, vertical datum and height definition
parameters.relationship: Tower height and storey count depend on where Z = 0 sits; CTBUH measures from the lowest significant open-air entrance. Z0 also needs a geodetic elevation and datum so City context and view limits stated as elevations line up.

parameters.name: Identity scheme (GlobalId, applicationId, own hash)
parameters.relationship: Stable ids let tags, versions and diffs survive re-import. IFC rooted entities carry a GlobalId; Speckle 2026.9 keys objects by applicationId (the older graph used content hashes). Layer 0 stores GlobalId, applicationId, its own SHA-256 and a UUID separately.

parameters.name: Internal frame (metres, Z-up, right-handed)
parameters.relationship: glTF fixes metres and +Y up, while Layer 0 is Z-up like Rhino and IFC authoring (convention, not checked here). The GLB exporter rotates the root node -90 degrees about X; a missed rotation lays the tower on its side and corrupts sun-direction tests.

parameters.name: IFC export baseline (IFC4 ADD2 vs IFC4X3)
parameters.relationship: IfcOpenShell states extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 TC1 and IFC4 Add2 TC1, while web-ifc enumerates IFC4X3. The default export is IFC4 ADD2; IFC4X3 is offered only after a tower round-trip passes in both libraries. Revit's exporter adds IFC4.3 views.

metrics.name: Mandatory-field completeness
metrics.good: 100% of required fields present (site polygon, Z0 geodetic elevation and datum, true-north record and north type, at least one tower, storeys with elevation, every volume with one tag)
metrics.bad: Any gap: dependent modules show a provisional label
metrics.method: JSON Schema validation on every write
metrics.basis: Required fields are our own schema v0 definition

metrics.name: IFC round-trip fidelity (v1)
metrics.good: 100% of ids, tags, units, axis assertion, plate-to-storey and zone-to-plate links survive IFC4 ADD2 export then re-import with IfcOpenShell and web-ifc; IFC4X3 reported separately
metrics.bad: Any tag, id, unit or link lost
metrics.method: Automated test on each test model, including a tower, diffing before and after
metrics.basis: Team test criterion; IFC4X3 geometry support unverified (IfcOpenShell README)

metrics.name: Mapping coverage
metrics.good: Every Layer 0 class has an IFC, Speckle 2026.9, glTF and BOT target documented
metrics.bad: Any class without a documented target
metrics.method: Coverage matrix generated from the mapping table
metrics.basis: Own mapping table; target schemas from the cited sources

visualization: Schema browser: tree Site > Podium/Tower > Level > Volume > FloorPlate with object counts
Coverage matrix: rows are Layer 0 classes, columns IFC / Speckle / glTF / BOT; green mapped, amber custom property set, red missing
Type badges on canvas node ports; clicking a badge opens the schema clause and its source
modules.method: Define Layer 0 as a JSON Schema (Z-up, right-handed, metres) with classes Site, Podium, Tower, Level (negative elevations below grade), ProgramVolume, FloorPlate, OpenSpace, Frontage (street type), AccessPoint (entrance, transit link, loading, parking), Viewpoint, ViewCone, ContextBuilding and Assumption. Geometry is metre triangle meshes plus an optional reference to exact source geometry. Mapping: Site to IfcSite and bot:Site; Podium and Tower to IfcBuilding and bot:Building; Level to IfcBuildingStorey and bot:Storey, elevation in the placement; ProgramVolume to IfcSpatialZone and bot:Zone (bot:intersectsZone to each storey); FloorPlate, cut by P14-M04, to IfcSpace and bot:Space; OpenSpace to an external IfcSpace under IfcSite. Tags become IfcClassificationReference, areas Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities, project flags a custom pset not named Pset_. Exporters are pure functions; CI re-imports every export with IfcOpenShell and web-ifc and diffs.
modules.human_judgment: Which tag a volume gets, which tags count as non-residential employment area, how storeys and the entrance Z0 are defined, and what counts toward FSR stay with the designer; the schema only records the decision and its origin.
modules.limits: Mapping massing volumes to IfcSpatialZone and IfcSpace is a convention. IFC4.3 clause pages were read; IFC4 ADD2 equivalents, IfcBuilding composition types and the direction of IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure were not. EXT_structural_metadata is a Cesium draft, so v0 uses plain glTF extras. BOT is a W3C community draft. Speckle 2026.9 replaced the object graph. Schema v0 will change after VTC test models.

modules.name: Multi-format import pipeline
modules.design_question: Which route gets each file type (.3dm, OBJ, IFC, glTF/FBX, DXF/DWG, SketchUp, Revit) into Layer 0 with units, hierarchy and metadata preserved, and what is lost on each?
modules.effort: L: core adapters .3dm, OBJ, GLB and IFC (web-ifc) plus SketchUp/Revit export cards about 5 person-days; FBX and DXF 2D route about 2; Speckle 2026.9 and APS routes about 4 more in v1 (team estimate)
inputs: Uploaded file (.3dm, .obj, .ifc/.ifczip, .glb/.gltf; v1: .fbx, .dxf; via export: .skp, .rvt, .dwg)
User-declared source unit (mandatory for OBJ)
Layer or name filter
Tessellation tolerance
outputs: Layer 0 draft: meshes, raw property bag per object, source provenance
Import report: objects read, skipped and why, units, warnings, objects with no render mesh
Source-file hash for P14-M06
Raw layer paths, names and IFC classes for P14-M04
Fixture manifest: organiser 'Site plans & 3D model' once obtained, plus 5 VTC-style test massings run in CI

parameters.name: Source unit
parameters.relationship: OBJ stores no unit, so a wrong guess scales the model by 1,000 (mm) or 3.28 (ft) and breaks the 244-305 m range. rhino3dm exposes ModelUnitSystem, glTF is metres, and SketchUp's OBJ export has a unit drop-down.

parameters.name: Tessellation tolerance and missing render meshes
parameters.relationship: Coarser tolerance gives fewer triangles but larger area and volume error on curved facades. The rhino3dm bindings read show only BrepFace.GetMesh, no Brep-to-mesh call, so B-reps (and probably extrusions and SubDs) need meshes saved in the file.

parameters.name: Import route per format
parameters.relationship: Native readers exist for 3dm, OBJ, IFC and glTF. SketchUp and Revit need a vendor export or connector, which adds a user step but keeps names, layers and properties. DWG/DXF 2D plans need a Rhino 8 conversion or a DXF parser.

parameters.name: IFC schema of the incoming file (2x3 / 4 / 4x3)
parameters.relationship: web-ifc enumerates IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3, but IfcOpenShell claims extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 and IFC4 Add2. Ask authors for IFC4 and do not send IFC4X3 to the server fallback until the round-trip spike passes.

parameters.name: Layer and name filter
parameters.relationship: Dropping furniture, annotation and context layers cuts triangles and mis-tagging; keeping everything preserves provenance but slows load and pollutes floor-area sums.

parameters.name: Metadata retention
parameters.relationship: Retained properties feed P14-M04 labelling. Connectors differ: Rhino sends name, colour, user strings; SketchUp custom attributes; Revit category, family, type, level and parameters.

parameters.name: Organiser model format (unknown)
parameters.relationship: The brief lists 'Site plans & 3D model' without formats. If it is .skp or .dwg, none of the core adapters reads it, so the format decides whether entrants need a Rhino 8 or SketchUp conversion step first.

metrics.name: Object accounting
metrics.good: 100% of source objects imported or listed as skipped with a reason
metrics.method: Count source objects against imported plus skipped
metrics.basis: Team rule: nothing disappears without a record

metrics.name: Volume parity with source application
metrics.good: <= 1% difference between imported mesh volume and source-reported volume
metrics.method: Compare signed mesh volume with the volume the user reads from Rhino, SketchUp or IFC quantities
metrics.basis: Team assumption; no source threshold found

metrics.name: IFC import time (<= 50 MB, mid-range laptop)
metrics.good: <= 10 s to meshes, in a worker
metrics.method: Time web-ifc open plus mesh extraction on a VTC-sized test model on a mid-range Windows laptop
metrics.basis: web-ifc benchmark on an Apple M1 (free RAM about 137, total 8192, units not stated): files of 26-70 MB opened in 0.17-1.16 s and executed in 0.52-7.6 s, and time does not track size (47 MB in 0.52 s, 34 MB in 7.6 s). Earlier quote picked a subset. Thresholds are padded presets to be replaced by our own measurement

metrics.name: UI responsiveness during import (INP p75)
metrics.method: Event timing while a worker imports
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Peak memory of an import
metrics.good: <= 50% of the WASM module's declared maximum memory
metrics.method: Compare memory.buffer.byteLength with the module's declared maximum, read from the WASM binary, during imports
metrics.basis: Team presets. Corrects the earlier 4 GiB wasm32 ceiling, which was general knowledge, not an opened page: Memory64 is stable in Chrome 133 and Firefox 134 but only a Safari Technical Preview, so Safari and each module's own maximum bind

visualization: Import report panel: one row per source object with status chips (imported, merged, skipped, no render mesh) and reason
Unit-detection banner showing candidate scales and the resulting selected-polygon bounding box against 79.2 x 144.8 m
3D preview coloured by import status (green ok, amber heuristic, red skipped) plus triangle count per layer bar chart
Dated supported-formats table in the import dialog; each row links to its how-to card and lists what is lost
modules.method: Sniff format, then run an adapter in a Web Worker that emits one intermediate ImportedObject list. .3dm: rhino3dm File3dm read, layer paths, object names and attributes, instance definitions, ModelUnitSystem, EarthAnchorPoint; use saved render meshes through BrepFace.GetMesh and list B-reps, extrusions and SubDs lacking them. IFC: web-ifc mesh streaming plus property sets for IFC2x3 and IFC4; IfcOpenShell server fallback for oversized files; IFC4X3 only after the spike. OBJ: parse groups and usemtl, require a unit. glTF/GLB: three.js GLTFLoader, read extras. FBX and DXF: v1, unit prompt. SKP and RVT: accept exported OBJ/GLB/IFC or Speckle versions with an export how-to card. The list then passes through P14-M03 (units, georeference) and P14-M05 (health) before it is written to Layer 0.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the source unit when detection is ambiguous, deciding which layers are building versus context or clutter, and accepting skipped objects.
modules.limits: Browsers cannot read .skp or .rvt: the SketchUp C SDK needs developer registration and Trimble terms; Revit is proprietary. McNeel says Rhino.Compute core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core-hour) is incompatible with Educational and Commercial licences; workstation use is unaddressed (unverified). OBJ loses hierarchy and metadata. Speckle connectors do not transfer image textures. Extrusion and SubD mesh access in rhino3dm is unconfirmed.

modules.name: Units, true north and georeferencing
modules.design_question: Where is the model, and which way is north? Fix units, anchor the site in EPSG:3157 with a geodetic Z0, reconcile the plan's rotated north arrow with true north.
modules.effort: S-M: core unit check, north-type confirmation, CRS and Z0 record about 2 person-days; IfcMapConversion export, parcel snapping and WMM declination about 1.5 more in v1 (team estimate)
inputs: Layer 0 draft and import report (declared units)
User-selected site polygon or tower object for scale detection
Site boundary polygon; optional City parcel polygons from P14-M08 for snapping
North-arrow bearing: two points clicked on the plan, or IFC TrueNorth, or Rhino ModelNorth
North type declared by the user: true, grid or magnetic
Any IfcMapConversion / IfcProjectedCRS in the file, Rhino EarthAnchorPoint, and the entrance-level Z0 geodetic elevation
outputs: Georeference record: crs EPSG:3157 (EPSG:26910 accepted as alias with a warning), realization and epoch, origin easting/northing, z0_geodetic_m, vertical_datum, true_north_deg, north_type, magnetic_declination_deg (model, date), grid_convergence_deg, ground_to_grid_scale, LoGeoRef level
Unit scale factor applied
Street-grid bearing estimate (deg from true north)
IfcMapConversion (OrthogonalHeight = Z0) and IfcProjectedCRS (VerticalDatum) for export; local-to-map 4x4 matrix
True-north vector for sun and wind modules, released only after north type is confirmed

parameters.name: Declared source unit
parameters.relationship: Scales every coordinate: a mm/m slip changes tower height 1,000-fold, ft/m 3.28-fold. Detection tests candidate scales on the user-selected site polygon or tower against 79.2 x 144.8 m, never the whole file, and the user confirms with one click.

parameters.name: North type (true, grid or magnetic)
parameters.relationship: The brief's north arrow is rotated relative to the street grid and its type is unstated. Treating a grid or magnetic arrow as true north rotates every sun, shadow and wind result by the difference, so CLIM modules stay blocked until the user confirms.

parameters.name: True-north angle (model north vs +Y)
parameters.relationship: Rotates every sun-path, shadow and wind result by the same angle. For a 300 m tower at latitude 49.29 N, 1 degree moves the shadow tip about 6 m at equinox noon and about 17 m at winter-solstice noon (derived).

parameters.name: Magnetic declination (WMM)
parameters.relationship: Declination at the site and date converts a magnetic arrow to true north. WMM2025 is valid until late 2029; the tool computes the value and records model and date. A size near 15 degrees east at Vancouver is informal and unverified.

parameters.name: Street-grid skew (grid bearing vs true north)
parameters.relationship: The downtown street grid is skewed from true north, so a model aligned to the grid must still carry true north separately or solar results rotate by the skew. It is derived from the dominant parcel-edge direction; its value is unresolved.

parameters.name: Horizontal CRS and datum
parameters.relationship: Use EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N, the frame of City LiDAR 2022. proj4js's NAD83 datum has towgs84 0,0,0, so EPSG:26910 applies no shift; EPSG gives the CSRS-to-WGS84 transformation accuracy as 1.0 m (alternative 2.0 m).

parameters.name: Z0 geodetic elevation and vertical datum
parameters.relationship: City footprint heights are geodetic and LiDAR uses CGVD28GVRD, and view limits are elevations, so Z0 must be stored as a geodetic height plus datum, not a bare local zero. Default it from LiDAR ground at the entrance; the user confirms.

parameters.name: Ground-to-grid scale
parameters.relationship: UTM scales distances by about 0.9996 near the zone centre, so areas shrink about 0.08%: roughly 83 m2 on the brief's 103,200 m2 minimum (derived). Compute areas in local ground units and store the scale for IfcMapConversion.

parameters.name: Model origin
parameters.relationship: UTM northings near 5.46 million m exceed float32 resolution (about 0.5 m steps, derived), so raw coordinates jitter in WebGL. A site-local origin keeps precision; three-mesh-bvh documents errors for large off-centre geometry.

metrics.name: Unit plausibility
metrics.good: Selected site polygon or tower within +/-2% of 79.2 x 144.8 m after scaling, and tower height inside 244-305 m
metrics.bad: Off by 3x or more, or tower height outside 244-305 m, signalling a unit error
metrics.method: Compare the selected polygon bounds with the brief site after each candidate scale; also test floor-to-floor against an editable 2.5-6 m preset (no source; typical values belong to the program and structure packets)
metrics.basis: Brief gives approximate size; the 2% tolerance and the floor-to-floor preset are team assumptions

metrics.name: True-north error
metrics.method: Difference between the plan's arrow bearing converted to true north (type and declination applied) and the confirmed true north (IFC TrueNorth, Rhino ModelNorth or user)
metrics.basis: Team presets. Derived: noon altitude = 90 - 49.29 - 23.44 = 17.3 deg at winter solstice, so a 300 m tower casts about 965 m and 1 degree moves the tip about 17 m; at equinox noon the shadow is about 349 m and the shift about 6 m; 0.25 degree gives about 1.5-4 m. The earlier 100 m shadow understated this about tenfold

metrics.name: North type confirmed
metrics.good: User has confirmed true, grid or magnetic and the declination or convergence is applied
metrics.method: Check the required georeference field before releasing the true-north vector
metrics.basis: Team rule; the brief gives no north type

metrics.name: Georeference level (LoGeoRef)
metrics.good: 50: IfcMapConversion plus IfcProjectedCRS (EPSG:3157 and vertical datum)
metrics.bad: 20 or lower: single latitude/longitude, no rotation
metrics.method: Inspect the IFC attributes present; emit IfcMapConversion on export
metrics.basis: Level definitions from the City2BIM wiki; the target level is a team choice

metrics.name: Site position agreement with City parcels
metrics.bad: > 2.0 m, which suggests a datum, unit or CRS mix-up
metrics.method: Distance between placed site corners and the nearest City parcel vertices, after reprojecting with EPSG:3157
metrics.basis: Presets set at the EPSG transformation accuracies (1.0 m default, 2.0 m alternative); parcels are 'not as precise' in places. Replaces the earlier 0.5 m target and the 2-4 m shift claim, which assumed EPSG:26910

metrics.name: Z0 agreement with City LiDAR ground
metrics.good: <= 1.0 m between confirmed Z0 and LiDAR ground at the entrance
metrics.bad: > 3.0 m, which suggests a datum or Z0 error
metrics.method: Sample LiDAR 2022 ground class at the site entrance and compare with the stated geodetic Z0
metrics.basis: Editable presets; LiDAR vertical accuracy 0.081 m at 95%, so metre-scale gaps are datum or Z0 errors, not noise

visualization: Plan view with four labelled arrows (true north, grid north, magnetic north, plan north) and their angles
Site outline over City parcel polygons with a distance heat-line
Unit-detection card listing candidate scales, and a LoGeoRef 10-50 badge with a checklist of IFC attributes present
Z0 card: local Z0, geodetic elevation and datum beside a LiDAR ground profile at the entrance
modules.method: 1) Units: rhino3dm ModelUnitSystem, IFC IfcUnitAssignment, glTF = metres, OBJ = ask. 2) Scale check on the user-selected site polygon or tower, not the whole file: test candidates (1, 0.001, 0.01, 0.3048, 0.0254) against 79.2 x 144.8 m within 2%, plus tower-height and floor-to-floor plausibility; the user always confirms. 3) CRS: register EPSG:3157 in proj4js with proj4.defs from the epsg.io string and test against a PROJ reference; accept EPSG:26910 input with a warning. 4) Z0: default from City LiDAR ground at the entrance, user confirms, store CGVD28GVRD or CGVD2013. 5) North: arrow bearing from two clicked points; require north type; compute WMM declination and grid convergence (about 0.09 degree, derived); derive street-grid bearing from parcel edges. 6) Emit IfcMapConversion (OrthogonalHeight = Z0) and IfcProjectedCRS (VerticalDatum); store float64, render relative to the origin.
modules.human_judgment: Confirming which north the site plan's arrow shows (true, grid or magnetic), choosing site origin, entrance level and Z0, and deciding whether to align the model to the street grid.
modules.limits: No source I could open gives the downtown street-grid skew or says which north the organiser's arrow shows; confirm with the organiser. The organiser's vertical datum and the datum name behind the footprint dataset's 'geodetic' heights are unknown. WMM declination and the EPSG:3157 registration were not computed or tested here. Georeferencing a hypothetical block is a convention, not a survey.

modules.name: Storey schedule, volume slicing and semantic labelling
modules.design_question: How do massing volumes and detailed models become per-storey floor plates and proposed program tags that a designer confirms, with evidence, confidence and an area cross-check?
modules.effort: M: core storey schedule UI, slicing and manual tagging about 3 person-days; detailed-model path 1.5; rules, LLM stage and review queue about 4 more in v1 (team estimate)
inputs: Layer 0 draft: closed ProgramVolumes and any imported storeys or slab faces
User storey schedule: ground-floor elevation (Z0), floor-to-floor height per program band, below-grade levels
Property bag per object (layer path, name, user strings, IFC class and psets)
Geometry summary (bounding box, area, normals, Z extents)
Layer 0 tag vocabulary; optional designer examples for few-shot prompts
Trust level from P14-M05 stage A (only closed volumes are sliced)
outputs: Level table {name, elevation, floor-to-floor, below_grade, origin: schedule | imported | detected}
FloorPlate records {volume_id, level_id, tag, gross_area, outline polygon} written to Layer 0
Plate-sum area cross-check per volume
ProposedTag list {object_id, tag, confidence, evidence[], origin rule|AI} and review queue (v1)
Accepted tags written to Layer 0 with tag_origin and confidence; result card names the path that ran

parameters.name: Storey schedule (floor-to-floor per program band)
parameters.relationship: A taller floor-to-floor in a band gives fewer plates within a fixed tower height and so less floor area; the schedule, not the mesh, sets storey count for massing. Typical values belong to the structure and program packets and are not sourced here.

parameters.name: Slicing method (mid-height slice vs band intersection)
parameters.relationship: A slice at mid-storey height gives plate area exactly for prismatic volumes but only approximates tapered or curved ones; intersecting each slab band and dividing volume by floor-to-floor tracks the taper. Manifold's C++ API offers slice and volume.

parameters.name: Zero-level definition (entrance floor)
parameters.relationship: Which level is ground changes storey numbering and tower height; CTBUH uses the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance, and below-grade levels get negative elevations.

parameters.name: Floor-detection Z tolerance and path gate
parameters.relationship: For detailed models only: a wider tolerance merges mezzanines and double-height floors, a narrower one splits sloped slabs. A single extrusion has only top and bottom faces, so detection needs at least 3 horizontal-face clusters; counting follows CTBUH.

parameters.name: Rule layer (IFC class and layer-name dictionary)
parameters.relationship: Deterministic rules explain themselves and cover well-labelled IFC/Revit exports; coverage falls for .3dm and OBJ with ad-hoc layer names, which is where the AI step is needed.

parameters.name: AI model and structured-output schema
parameters.relationship: A schema-constrained reply guarantees parseable tags with evidence strings, not correct ones. The API cannot enforce numeric min/max (SDK helpers validate locally), and refusals or truncation can break the schema, so confidence gating and human confirmation are required.

parameters.name: Auto-accept confidence threshold
parameters.relationship: A higher threshold gives fewer wrong auto-tags but more manual confirmations; items below it go to the review queue. Values are team assumptions until calibrated on a labelled set.

parameters.name: Hosted-API data handling
parameters.relationship: Sending names and layer text to a hosted model exposes project information. Anthropic states API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days by default, with zero retention only by agreement; the tool is opt-in per project with a rules-only mode.

metrics.name: Plate-sum area cross-check
metrics.good: <= 0.5% difference between the sum of plate area x floor-to-floor and the volume's own volume
metrics.method: Compare manifold volume of each ProgramVolume with the sum over its FloorPlates
metrics.basis: Team presets; prismatic volumes should agree to rounding, tapered ones show the mid-height slice error

metrics.name: Storey count error vs author's count
metrics.method: Scheduled or detected storeys (CTBUH counting) minus the count the author states
metrics.basis: Counting rule from CTBUH; thresholds are team assumptions (off by one shown amber)

metrics.name: Tag precision on a gold set (v1)
metrics.good: >= 95% for auto-accepted tags
metrics.method: Hold-out set of team-labelled models (including VTC test massings)
metrics.basis: No literature benchmark retrieved; editable preset

metrics.good: 100% of enclosed floor area tagged and confirmed
metrics.method: Tagged plate area divided by total plate area
metrics.basis: Team rule

metrics.name: Human override rate (v1)
metrics.good: <= 10% of AI tags changed by the user
metrics.method: Changed tags divided by AI-proposed tags per project

visualization: 3D view: each ProgramVolume cut by translucent storey planes with elevation ticks and labels; plates coloured by tag, opacity or hatch showing confidence
Level x tag area table with employment-flagged tags outlined, totals per tag, and a plate-sum error badge per volume (green <= 0.5%, red > 2%)
Review table sorted by lowest confidence; click zooms to the object with an evidence popover (for example 'layer L12_OFFICE matched rule R3')
modules.method: Path A (massing, default): the user enters a storey schedule (Z0, floor-to-floor per program band, below-grade levels). Each closed ProgramVolume is cut by manifold-3d at those elevations into FloorPlate records with outline, gross area and tag, and plate areas times storey heights are compared with the volume. Path B (detailed IFC/Revit): read IfcBuildingStorey or Revit levels; if absent and at least 3 horizontal-face clusters exist, cluster slab Z values into storeys. Tagging: stage 1 rules (IFC class, Revit category, layer-path tokens via an editable dictionary); stage 2 candidate cores from vertical stacks of near-identical footprints; stage 3 (v1) LLM for unresolved items, schema-constrained tag, confidence and evidence from names and layers only; stage 4 human review queue. Labels outside the vocabulary go to 'unclassified'. Every AI call logs model id, prompt hash and output for P14-M06.
modules.human_judgment: The storey schedule, the entrance zero level and every tag are the designer's decisions; rules and AI only propose. Ambiguous uses (hotel lobby versus public space, amenity versus residential) remain a judgement.
modules.limits: Slicing needs closed manifold volumes and horizontal storey bands; split-level (partial) storeys are not handled in v1. No labelling accuracy benchmark was retrieved, so thresholds are team assumptions until measured on a labelled VTC set. The 3-cluster gate is our assumption. LLM output varies with model version; hosted-API use raises confidentiality questions for competition entries. manifold JS method names are unverified.

modules.name: Geometry health and Layer 0 validation
modules.design_question: Is the imported geometry closed, correctly scaled, inside plausible brief limits and tagged completely enough for evaluation modules to trust? What exactly fails, and where?
modules.effort: S-M: core closed-volume, scale and envelope checks (stage A) about 2 person-days; overlap and gap Booleans (stage B) about 2 more in v1 (team estimate)
inputs: Layer 0 draft
Import report
Georeference record
Site boundary polygon
FloorPlate records from P14-M04 (optional, stage B only)
outputs: Health report: severity, location and suggested fix per rule
Trust level per downstream input (pass / warn / block)
Brief precheck table (tower height under three conventions, site size, per-tag floor area)
Auto-fix actions (weld, flip normals, rescale)

parameters.name: Weld tolerance
parameters.relationship: Larger tolerance closes small gaps but collapses thin features; too small leaves open edges that make volume and floor area wrong.

parameters.name: Closed-volume requirement by class
parameters.relationship: ProgramVolumes must be closed for volume and area to be valid; context surfaces and site plates may stay open without affecting shadow or wind results.

parameters.name: Brief envelope (height 244-305 m, site 79.2 x 144.8 m)
parameters.relationship: Heights or site sizes outside the envelope usually signal unit or zero-level mistakes. The brief allows justified breaches, so flags warn rather than block.

parameters.name: Height measurement convention
parameters.relationship: One tower reads different heights: CTBUH entrance to architectural top, geodetic top elevation (Z0 plus height), or height above the City by-law base surface (definition not read). Showing all three makes the 244-305 m check state its convention.

parameters.name: Overlap and gap tolerance between program volumes (stage B)
parameters.relationship: Overlaps double-count floor area and gaps hide it; the tolerance sets what is flagged and therefore how reliable per-use area and FSR inputs are.

parameters.name: Analysis triangle budget
parameters.relationship: More triangles improve accuracy but slow BVH queries; three-mesh-bvh quotes 500 rays at 60 fps on an 80,000-polygon model as a reference scale.

metrics.name: Closed-manifold share of ProgramVolumes
metrics.bad: Any open volume feeding area or volume metrics
metrics.method: Edge-use count (each edge shared by exactly two faces); Brep.IsSolid and IsManifold for .3dm
metrics.basis: Team rule; rhino3dm binds IsSolid and IsManifold

metrics.name: Tower height (shown under three conventions)
metrics.good: 244-305 m under the active convention (default: CTBUH entrance to architectural top, excluding antennas and signage)
metrics.bad: Outside the range (warn; a justified breach may be rewarded)
metrics.method: CTBUH: Z of architectural top minus Z of the lowest significant open-air entrance floor; geodetic: Z0 plus that height; by-law base-surface height only when the user enters it
metrics.basis: UNVERIFIED: the 244-305 m range comes from the project packet; the brief PDF was not opened (P14-S54 opened=false) and its measurement convention is unknown. Corrected from a wrongly assigned 'verified' status. The CTBUH rule itself is sourced

metrics.name: Site bounding-box match
metrics.good: Within 2% of 79.2 x 144.8 m
metrics.method: Compare site polygon bounds with the brief
metrics.basis: Brief gives approximate size; tolerances are team assumptions

metrics.name: Program overlap volume (stage B, v1)
metrics.good: <= 0.1% of total program volume
metrics.method: Mesh Boolean intersection of volumes within each storey
metrics.basis: Team assumption

metrics.name: Tag coverage of enclosed volume
metrics.method: Tagged enclosed volume divided by total enclosed volume
metrics.basis: Team rule

visualization: 3D overlay: open edges red lines, flipped faces magenta, overlap volumes orange, out-of-envelope parts hatched
Checklist of pass/warn/block rules, each linked to its source clause (for example 'VTC brief: 244-305 m')
Height card: three bars (CTBUH, geodetic, by-law base) against the 244-305 m band
Trust badge on each downstream node input
modules.method: Run in a worker. Stage A, before slicing: (1) edge-use histogram, where every edge shared by exactly two faces means closed and manifold, and IsSolid/IsManifold for .3dm B-reps; (2) signed volume sign to detect inverted normals; (3) degenerate and duplicate faces; (4) unit sanity and brief envelope, with height reported under three conventions (CTBUH from the user-confirmed entrance floor to the architectural top, geodetic top, City base surface when entered). Stage B, after P14-M04 (v1): (5) program overlap and gap per storey with manifold mesh Booleans; (6) tag coverage ratio. Each rule returns severity, location and fix. 'Block' stops dependent modules; 'warn' lets them run with a provisional label shown on every result card.
modules.human_judgment: Deciding whether an open or overlapping volume is a modelling error or design intent, and whether an out-of-envelope result is a justified breach.
modules.limits: Mesh checks cannot prove design intent; open context meshes are legitimate. The brief says its documents are academic and the jury may reward justified breaches, so envelope flags are warnings. The CTBUH rule needs the user to identify the lowest significant entrance. The brief's own height convention and the by-law base-surface definition were not read.

modules.name: Design-state versioning, provenance ledger and anonymised export
modules.design_question: How are design states, assumptions and module results stored so any result can be reproduced, compared, forked and traced to sources, including flagged false assumptions that must stay visible?
modules.effort: M: snapshots, hashing and result cards about 4 person-days (minimal provenance fields ship in P14-M01 for core); anonymised export about 1.5; diff view about 4; fork and merge about 5 (team estimate)
inputs: Layer 0 document and geometry blobs
Module graph configuration (nodes on/off, parameter values, assumption overrides)
Module outputs and source ids
Author and timestamp
Anonymise flag and pseudonym
outputs: Snapshot ids (content hash) with parent links
Diff {objects added/removed/changed, tag changes, parameter changes}
Provenance graph of Entity, Activity and Agent
Result cards: 'computed from snapshot X, module vY, parameters Z'
Append-only assumption log including FALSE ASSUMPTION flags
Anonymised export package plus a residual-identifier scan report

parameters.name: Snapshot granularity (per edit / per module run / manual commit)
parameters.relationship: Finer snapshots give exact undo and reproducibility but multiply storage and noise; manual commits are cheap but results may refer to uncommitted state, so every result card must pin a snapshot.

parameters.name: Hashing and canonical form
parameters.relationship: Content hashes deduplicate identical states and expose silent changes. Speckle's older graph used content identity; 2026.9 keys objects by applicationId, so Layer 0 computes its own SHA-256. Unsorted JSON keys or unrounded floats break hashes unless canonicalised.

parameters.name: Storage backend (Speckle / git-in-browser / custom)
parameters.relationship: Speckle brings versions, viewer and connectors, but its format changed at 2026.9 and the Free plan keeps 100 versions with 30-day history. Browser git is free but needs a CORS proxy for clone and push and can reorder writes.

parameters.name: Module version pinning
parameters.relationship: Forked modules may change thresholds. Without module version and threshold sources stored on each result, a diff of metrics cannot tell a design change from a rule change.

parameters.name: Assumption log retention
parameters.relationship: Entries move team assumption to verified or FALSE ASSUMPTION but are never deleted; deletion would hide why earlier results changed. This is a project requirement, not an external standard.

parameters.name: Merge model (snapshot fork vs real-time sync)
parameters.relationship: Snapshot fork and three-way merge matches GitHub-like community forking and is simpler; real-time CRDT sync merges concurrent edits automatically but needs per-object conflict rules and is deferred.

parameters.name: Anonymised export (identifier stripping)
parameters.relationship: VTC entries are evaluated anonymously. The IFC header FILE_NAME carries author and organization, IfcOwnerHistory (optional in IFC4) names people and applications, and Speckle versions carry an author; the export blanks or pseudonymises each and the ledger keeps real identity locally.

metrics.name: Reproducibility
metrics.good: 100% of deterministic results regenerate with an identical output hash from snapshot plus module version
metrics.method: Nightly replay of stored result cards
metrics.basis: Course requirement to show work; threshold is a team rule

metrics.name: Provenance completeness
metrics.good: 100% of displayed numbers link to a source id and snapshot, or carry a 'team assumption' badge
metrics.bad: Any unsourced number without a badge
metrics.method: Scan result cards for missing source_ids
metrics.basis: Course requirement (every result cites its source)

metrics.name: UI latency while snapshotting or diffing (INP p75)
metrics.method: Run hashing and diff in workers; measure event timing
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Residual identifiers in anonymised export
metrics.good: 0 found in IFC header and OwnerHistory, GLB asset and extras, Speckle author, PROV agents, file paths and image EXIF
metrics.method: Automated scan of every exported file after pseudonymisation
metrics.basis: Team rule derived from the VTC anonymity statement; the brief PDF was not opened

visualization: Commit graph (git-style DAG) coloured by author and fork
Two-snapshot diff: 3D ghost overlay (added green, removed red, moved amber) with a table of parameter and metric deltas
Result card chain source > snapshot > module version > metric, drawn with PROV-style arrows; FALSE ASSUMPTION entries in the special colour on the timeline
Anonymise dialog listing each scrubbed field before and after, with a pass/fail scan badge
modules.method: Canonicalise Layer 0 JSON (sorted keys, floats rounded to 1e-6 m) and hash geometry blobs (SHA-256). A snapshot is a Merkle-style manifest {layer0_hash, geometry_hashes, graph_config_hash, assumptions_hash, parent_ids, author, time}. Diff by object id: added and removed sets, per-object hashes, then attribute diffs (tag, storey, transform). Results are stored as PROV-O: a result Entity wasGeneratedBy a module-run Activity that used the snapshot and sources, wasAttributedTo an Agent. Forks copy manifest pointers; merge is three-way with conflicts listed for a human. Anonymised export blanks FILE_NAME author and organization, omits OwnerHistory, replaces Speckle author, PROV agents and file paths with a pseudonym, then scans outputs for residual identifiers. Optionally push snapshots to Speckle via specklepy; use ifcdiff for IFC comparison.
modules.human_judgment: When to commit, how to name a design state, resolving merge conflicts, deciding when an assumption has been disproved and must be flagged, and whether an export is safe to share.
modules.limits: Hash reproducibility holds only for deterministic modules; WASM or browser floating-point differences and LLM steps (P14-M04) break bit-exactness, so those results store the produced output. Speckle Free keeps 100 versions and 30 days. The VTC submission is four image boards, so board PDF/PNG metadata is handled in PRES; this scrubber covers shared model files and community forks. Real-time co-editing is out of scope.

modules.name: Browser geometry kernel and performance budget
modules.design_question: Which in-browser and optional server geometry stack handles tower-scale models fast enough for interactive evaluation, and when must work move to a worker, a server or Rhino.Compute?
modules.effort: S-M: core shell, workers, float64 store and performance HUD about 2.5 person-days; OpenCascade and Compute integration roadmap (team estimate)
inputs: Layer 0 meshes
Compute requests from modules (ray casts, sections, Booleans, area and volume)
Device capability and file size
outputs: Render mesh with LOD and analysis mesh with BVH
Section polylines and Boolean results
Performance report (ms, MB per node)
Offload-recommended flag per task

parameters.name: Tessellation tolerance and LOD
parameters.relationship: Coarser meshes speed ray casting for sun and view modules but understate curved-facade area; three-mesh-bvh's 500 rays at 60 fps on 80,000 polygons is a reference scale for analysis meshes.

parameters.name: Compute location (main thread / worker / server / Rhino.Compute)
parameters.relationship: Main-thread work over 50 ms hurts responsiveness; workers keep the canvas interactive. Rhino.Compute adds exact Rhino geometry but needs Rhino 8 for Windows; McNeel says core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core-hour) is incompatible with Educational licences; workstation use is unaddressed.

parameters.name: Kernel choice (mesh vs B-rep vs rhino3dm)
parameters.relationship: Mesh kernels (three.js, three-mesh-bvh, manifold) are small and fast but approximate. OCCT-based opencascade.js gives exact B-rep and STEP but its WASM is large; rhino3dm reads Rhino data but has no Brep meshing call in the bindings checked.

parameters.name: Numeric precision (float64 store, origin-relative render)
parameters.relationship: UTM northings near 5.46 million m exceed float32's 0.5 m resolution (derived); subtracting a site origin before upload keeps sub-millimetre precision at tower scale.

parameters.name: Memory ceiling and streaming
parameters.relationship: In practice each WASM module's declared maximum memory, not a browser-wide 4 GiB, is the limit, to be read per module. Memory64 is stable in Chrome and Firefox but only a Safari preview. City LiDAR tiles reach 2.74 GB zipped, so COPC range requests are used.

metrics.name: Input latency (INP, p75)
metrics.method: PerformanceObserver event timing during imports and slider drags
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Frame work per frame
metrics.good: <= 10 ms (16 ms budget at 60 fps)
metrics.method: Render stats and performance marks while orbiting the model
metrics.basis: RAIL: produce frames in 10 ms because the browser needs about 6 ms

metrics.name: Task chunk length
metrics.good: <= 50 ms chunks
metrics.method: Long Task observer
metrics.basis: RAIL: idle work in 50 ms chunks, respond within 100 ms

metrics.name: Canvas shell interactive (no model loaded)
metrics.good: <= 5 s on mid-range mobile over slow 3G; later loads < 2 s
metrics.method: Lighthouse; lazy-load rhino3dm, web-ifc and OCCT WASM after the shell
metrics.basis: RAIL load target

metrics.name: Peak WASM heap
metrics.good: <= 50% of the module's declared maximum memory
metrics.method: Sample memory.buffer.byteLength against the module's declared maximum, per module and per browser (Safari first)
metrics.basis: Team presets. Replaces the earlier 4 GiB wasm32 ceiling (general knowledge, unopened), which was unreachable as a bad threshold because a module stops at its own maximum

visualization: Performance HUD in the canvas corner (fps, frame ms, long-task count, heap MB and % of declared max) with traffic-light bands from the thresholds
Per-node timing bar on each canvas node showing parse, mesh, BVH and compute time
Offload banner naming the task and the measured cost when a threshold is crossed
modules.method: Parse in a worker (rhino3dm, web-ifc) into a Float64 geometry store, subtract the site origin, and upload Float32 buffers to three.js BufferGeometry. Build an analysis mesh with decimation and a three-mesh-bvh tree. Modules call workers by RPC for ray casts (sun, view), section planes, area and volume. Use manifold-3d for mesh Booleans, slicing and validation; lazy-load opencascade.js (custom build) only when a module needs exact B-rep or STEP. Offload rule: if a task exceeds 100 ms measured, or a file exceeds the tested size, move it to a server worker running IfcOpenShell or rhino3dm.py; use Rhino.Compute only if a licensed server exists. Record timings with PerformanceObserver (longtask, event timing) and memory against each module's declared maximum.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing speed versus accuracy (tessellation, offloading) and accepting approximations on curved geometry.
modules.limits: The opencascade.js repo page shows an OCCT 7.6.2 badge and no listed releases, so maintenance is unclear and its bundle is large unless custom-built (unverified). McNeel calls rhino3dm.wasm fairly large. Benchmarks quoted are on an Apple M1 and will not match student laptops. Rhino.Compute needs Windows and Rhino 8; whether workstation use is allowed for students is unverified.

modules.name: City of Vancouver context ingest, view cones and viewpoints
modules.design_question: What surrounding buildings, terrain and protected views can City open data supply, how current and accurate are they, and what must be added by hand, such as approved towers?
modules.effort: S-M: footprints, parcels and view cones about 4.5 person-days; LiDAR to COPC pipeline about 1 week, roadmap (team estimate). Skip if the organiser's 3D model already includes context.
inputs: Site location and EPSG:3157 georeference with Z0 from P14-M03
Context radius
Organiser's context model, if provided
Selected City datasets
User-entered viewpoints and view-limit elevations (with source and status)
outputs: ContextBuilding list {footprint, base_elev, top_elev, parts, source dataset, year, licence}
Terrain surface
ViewCone records {polygon, viewpoint_xyz, limit_elevation_m, limit_source, limit_status} for the 24 polygons
Viewpoint objects (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city) shared with PRES
Parcel polygons and rapid transit lines
Context currency report
Manual-add queue for approved towers

parameters.name: Context radius
parameters.relationship: A larger radius adds distant towers that cast long shadows or channel wind but increases triangles and download. The radius needed as a function of tower height is not sourced here and belongs to the CLIM packets.

parameters.name: Height source (footprints 2009 / LiDAR 2022 / organiser model / OSM and Overture)
parameters.relationship: Footprints derive from 2009 LiDAR and are not updated, so towers built since are missing. LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2, 0.081 m vertical accuracy at 95%) catches them but needs processing; Overture and OSM add newer footprints under ODbL.

parameters.name: Part handling (one building id, several polygons)
parameters.relationship: A building appears as stacked polygons with different base and top elevations. Extruding each from baseelev_m to topelev_m reproduces podium plus tower; maxht_m is the maximum over all parts of the building, so use it only for building-level summaries.

parameters.name: Coordinate frame and vertical datum of City data
parameters.relationship: LiDAR 2022 is NAD83(CSRS) UTM 10 with CGVD28GVRD heights; footprint heights are 'geodetic' without a named datum, and the parcel and footprint pages state no CRS. Reproject with EPSG:3157 and shift heights by Z0 to the local frame.

parameters.name: Manual additions (approved, unbuilt towers)
parameters.relationship: The brief says context includes future approved towers; no open dataset of approved massing was found, so omitting them under-predicts shadow and wind interaction.

parameters.name: Protected view cones and limit elevations (24 polygons)
parameters.relationship: Building heights inside cones are limited, but the dataset gives polygons only, no height fields. The tool intersects the tower footprint with each polygon and compares its geodetic top with a hand-entered limit; with no limit entered the result is 'unchecked'.

parameters.name: Viewpoints (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city)
parameters.relationship: The brief asks for a skyline view from Queen Elizabeth Park and a mid-city view. The dataset has four Queen Elizabeth Park cones (3.2.1-3.2.4) but no viewpoint coordinates, so position and direction are entered and stored as Viewpoint objects for PRES.

parameters.name: Licence and attribution
parameters.relationship: City data is under Open Government Licence - Vancouver; OSM-derived layers are ODbL (share-alike). The tool must show attribution and keep ODbL layers separable.

metrics.name: Data age
metrics.good: <= 5 years
metrics.method: 2026 minus acquisition year: footprints 2009 = 17 (bad), LiDAR 2022 = 4 (good)
metrics.basis: Team assumption; ages from dataset metadata

metrics.name: Stated vertical accuracy
metrics.good: Published and <= 0.2 m (LiDAR 2022: 0.081 m at 95%)
metrics.bad: Not stated (footprints 2009: 'approximate, best used for comparison')
metrics.method: Read from dataset metadata
metrics.basis: Team assumption; values quoted from City metadata

metrics.name: Missed tall buildings
metrics.good: 0 buildings taller than 100 m (LiDAR building class) without a matching footprint part
metrics.method: Compare LiDAR 2022 building-class heights with footprint extrusions and list unmatched peaks
metrics.basis: Team assumption; 100 m cut-off is an editable preset

metrics.name: Attribution completeness
metrics.good: 100% of context layers carry dataset id, licence and year
metrics.method: Check metadata on each context object
metrics.basis: Licence terms of the cited datasets (full City licence text not opened)

metrics.name: View-cone check status
metrics.good: Every cone polygon touching the site has a hand-entered limit elevation with source and status, and the tower's geodetic top is at or below it
metrics.bad: A touching cone with no limit entered ('unchecked'), or the top above the limit
metrics.method: 2D polygon intersection of site footprint with the 24 cones, then comparison of Z0 plus tower height with the entered limit
metrics.basis: Team logic; the dataset has no height fields and the by-laws are authoritative, so limit values stay hand-entered and are not sourced here

visualization: Context massing extruded from City data, coloured by data year (cool recent, warm old), with a ring at the chosen radius
View-cone polygons as translucent ground wedges with labels and a pass/unchecked/fail chip; LiDAR-derived terrain as hillshade
Viewpoint markers with a camera frustum for the Queen Elizabeth Park and mid-city views
Badge per layer showing source, licence and age; suspected missing towers as dashed outlines
modules.method: Fetch GeoJSON from the City open-data API (building-footprints-2009, property-parcel-polygons, view-cones, rapid-transit-lines) within the radius; check the coordinates actually returned, then reproject with proj4js (EPSG:3157 registered); group by bldgid; extrude each part from baseelev_m to topelev_m, check topelev_m minus baseelev_m equals hgt_agl, and shift heights by Z0 into the local frame. Render relative to the site origin. View cones: intersect the site footprint with the 24 polygons and compare the tower's geodetic top with any hand-entered limit. Roadmap: convert LiDAR 2022 LAS tiles (up to 2.74 GB zipped) to COPC server-side to update heights and detect new towers. Merge the organiser's context model with priority if supplied; users add approved towers as boxes tagged 'manual, team assumption'.
modules.human_judgment: Which context matters, adding approved-but-unbuilt towers, entering view-limit elevations from the by-laws, placing the viewpoints, and deciding whether to trust an old dataset over the organiser's model.
modules.limits: Footprints 2009 are generalised and not updated; towers completed since are absent or wrong. The view-cone dataset has polygons only: allowable height surfaces are in by-laws, and the City's view pages returned HTTP 403. The vertical datum name behind topelev_m is not stated beyond 'geodetic'. The City licence text and the Higher Buildings policy PDFs could not be opened.

sources.extract: IfcSpace: associated to a building storey, or to a site for exterior spaces; Pset_SpaceCommon carries IsExternal; page does not address multi-storey spaces. IfcSpatialZone: non-hierarchical, potentially overlapping functional grouping; linked to elements and spaces by IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure. IfcBuildingStorey: linked to its building by IfcRelAggregates; Elevation deprecated in IFC4.3 (use placement and Pset_BuildingStoreyCommon); CompositionType ELEMENT/COMPLEX/PARTIAL. Direction of the relationship and IFC4 ADD2 equivalents not confirmed.

sources.title: Speckle data schema overview (pre-2026.9 object graph, historical)
sources.extract: States it describes versions published before 2026.9. Objects identified by content hash for deduplication; applicationId gives stable version tracking; Collections hold hierarchy; DataObject displayValue holds visual meshes; a version is an immutable snapshot. Historical for design decisions.

sources.title: Speckle object model overview (2026.9 bundles) and relations page
sources.extract: Columnar property store plus relational layer, no root object; units per object; no Level object (ON_LEVEL relation), no Proxy types (HAS_MATERIAL replaces material proxies); other relations IN_SYSTEM, SUBELEMENT, CONNECTS_TO, containers IN_COLLECTION/IN_MODEL/IN_GROUP; objects keyed by applicationId (pages do not mention content hashes); site/building containers not described; pre-2026.9 SDKs get a 404 on new versions; send3/receive3; compatibility mode for ACC sync and file uploads until 1 November 2026.

sources.title: Speckle Revit connector
sources.extract: Revit 2023-2027, Windows only; exports model categories with family, type, level, parameters and meshes; image textures not transferred; objects load as Direct Shapes; licence and cost not covered.

sources.title: Speckle SketchUp connector
sources.extract: SketchUp 2021-2026 on Windows and macOS; publishes components, groups, faces, lines, custom attributes and render materials; image textures not supported.

sources.title: Speckle Rhino connector
sources.extract: Rhino 7 and 8, Windows only; sends geometry with name, colour, material and user strings, blocks, layer structure; image textures not transferred; brep conversion not documented on the page.

sources.title: Speckle pricing

sources.title: speckle-server repository
sources.extract: Apache-2.0 unless stated; monorepo with server, frontend, three.js viewer, objectloader and file-import service; Docker Compose files for self-hosting.

sources.title: glTF 2.0 specification
sources.extract: Units for all linear distances are metres; right-handed coordinate system with +Y up and +Z forward (first 200,000 characters read; extras text not seen).

sources.title: EXT_structural_metadata (glTF extension, Cesium draft)
sources.extract: Status line: Draft; contributors mostly Cesium; page does not claim Khronos ratification. The Khronos glTF main repo's Vendor listing (extensions/2.0/Vendor) does not contain it, and a guessed canonical path returned 404, so v0 uses plain glTF extras.

sources.title: Building Topology Ontology (BOT)
sources.publisher: W3C Linked Building Data Community Group
sources.extract: Classes Site, Building, Storey, Space, Zone, Element, Interface; Zone is the superclass; hasStorey and hasSpace sub-properties of containsZone; intersectsZone relates zones whose 3D extents intersect (stairwell across storeys is the example, though the page's own example uses an extension sub-property); alignment to ifcOWL provided; no licence stated.

sources.title: rhino3dm repository
sources.extract: MIT; .NET, Python (CPython 3.8-3.14) and JavaScript/WASM; reads and writes .3dm, layers and attributes; client for Rhino Compute; .wasm is fairly large per the JS README.

sources.title: rhino3dm bindings (settings, brep, mesh, layer)

sources.extract: Metres; 126 W to 120 W; central meridian 123 W; scale factor 0.9996; PROJ string has towgs84=0,0,0; remark: for accuracies better than 1 m replaced by NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 10N in Canada; default transformation to WGS84 listed at 4.0 m accuracy (code 1188), remarks say 2 m per axis.

sources.title: Transverse Mercator projection (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Convergence gamma = arctan(tan(lambda) sin(phi)); point scale k0 / sqrt(1 - sin^2 lambda cos^2 phi).

sources.title: proj4js (repository and lib/constants/Datum.js)
sources.extract: JS port of PROJ; predefines EPSG 4326, 4269, 3857 and WGS84 UTM zones 32601-32660 and 32701-32760 (not 26910 or 3157); custom definitions via proj4.defs; accepts WKT and PROJJSON; licence not named on the page. Datum.js (read 21 Oct 2026): the nad83 entry has towgs84 '0,0,0' and there is no NAD83 CSRS entry.

sources.title: CTBUH height criteria
sources.publisher: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat
sources.extract: Height from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance; architectural top excludes antennas and signage; floors counted above ground including significant mezzanines and major mechanical floors, excluding plant above the general roof.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: Building footprints 2009
sources.extract: Open Government Licence - Vancouver; 124,181 polygons derived from 2009 LiDAR; 'approximate, best used for comparison, not updated'. Schema: baseelev_m and topelev_m lowest/highest elevation (geodetic, datum not named); hgt_agl essentially topelev minus baseelev; avght_m average height of the element; maxht_m and minht_m max/min over all elements sharing BLDGID; base_m base elevation of all elements sharing BLDGID. Sample building 149845: base 30.7, top 219.29, hgt_agl 188.59, maxht_m 208.63.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: LiDAR 2022
sources.extract: Acquired 7 and 9 Sep 2022; about 49 points/m2; vertical accuracy 0.081 m at 95%; 181 LAS tiles from 16.45 MB to 2.74 GB zipped; horizontal NAD 83 (CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD in UTM 10, portal grid map in WGS 84; vertical CGVD28GVRD; Metro Vancouver Geoid listed; building class 6 inferred from list position.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: Property parcel polygons

sources.title: EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 10N
sources.extract: Area 126 W to 120 W, British Columbia, NWT, Yukon; datum NAD83(CSRS) on GRS 1980; 2D projected CRS with no vertical axis; PROJ string +proj=utm +zone=10 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=-0.991,1.9072,0.5129,-1.25033e-07,-4.6785e-08,-5.6529e-08,0; default transformation to WGS 84 code 1946 accuracy 1.0 m (approximation ignoring time-dependent parameters), alternative code 1842 accuracy 2.0 m, where NAD83(CSRS) can be considered coincident with WGS 84 for many purposes.

sources.title: IFC 4.3 IfcMapConversion and IfcProjectedCRS (GitHub docs)
sources.extract: IfcMapConversion: Eastings, Northings, OrthogonalHeight (relative to the vertical datum specified), XAxisAbscissa/XAxisOrdinate for rotation, Scale (default 1.0, applies to x, y, z). IfcProjectedCRS: Name, GeodeticDatum, VerticalDatum (needed for 3D systems when Name does not define it), MapProjection, MapZone, MapUnit.

sources.title: IFC 4.3 property, quantity, classification and root pages (GitHub docs)
sources.extract: Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities: GrossFloorArea, GrossPerimeter, Height, NetFloorArea, NetVolume. IfcPropertySet: user-defined sets must not use the Pset_ prefix. IfcClassificationReference: Identification, Name, ReferencedSource (lightweight or full classification). IfcRoot: GlobalId; OwnerHistory optional in IFC4. Pset_SpaceCommon page lists IsExternal but not its other properties.

sources.title: ISO 10303-21 (STEP-File) header structure (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: HEADER holds FILE_DESCRIPTION, FILE_NAME and FILE_SCHEMA; FILE_NAME has name, time_stamp, author, organization, preprocessor_version, originating_system, authorization; apart from time_stamp and FILE_SCHEMA fields may be left empty.

sources.title: NOAA NCEI World Magnetic Model
sources.extract: WMM2025 epoch 2025.0, valid until late 2029 (expires 31 Dec 2029); software outputs an uncertainty per component; no declination value for Vancouver was computed or retrieved (NOAA calculator API returned HTTP 400, NRCan page describes only a manual method).

sources.title: Anthropic privacy centre: data retention for API inputs and outputs
sources.extract: Inputs and outputs for API users are deleted from the backend within 30 days by default, with exceptions (longer retention you control, agreed terms, Usage Policy enforcement, legal requirements); zero retention only by agreement; page does not state training use.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver building footprints and heights can serve as a current context model
flags.correction: The dataset 'Building footprints 2009' is derived from 2009 LiDAR, 'approximate, best used for comparison' and 'not being updated'. Use LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2) or the organiser's 3D model for current heights.
flags.detail: Data age of footprints is 17 years against 4 years for LiDAR 2022; towers built since 2009 are missing or wrong. See P14-M08.

flags.claim: Rhino can import or export IFC natively, so IFC is a universal route from .3dm
flags.detail: McNeel's Rhino 8 and Rhino 9 import/export indexes list skp, glb/gltf, obj, fbx, dwg and step, but not ifc or rvt. The page notes dialogs show only formats whose plug-ins are enabled, so a plug-in route may exist; not confirmed.

flags.claim: Rhino.Compute can be used by the student team for server-side geometry
flags.detail: Code is MIT but runs on Rhino 8 for Windows. McNeel's page says core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core per hour) is not compatible with Educational or Commercial licences, cannot be enabled on a team containing licences, and is required on Windows Server-based systems; it does not address workstation use. Whether the course or UBC holds a suitable licence is unknown, so Compute stays optional and not core.

flags.claim: proj4js can transform EPSG:3157 (or 26910) out of the box
flags.correction: proj4js predefines WGS84 UTM zones (EPSG 32601-32660) and a few others, not 26910 or 3157; the module must register the NAD83(CSRS) UTM zone 10N definition with proj4.defs from the epsg.io string. Do not use +datum=NAD83, which proj4js defines with towgs84 0,0,0.
flags.detail: Based on the proj4js repository page and Datum.js; the registered definition has not been tested against a PROJ reference result.

flags.claim: SketchUp .skp can be read directly with the SketchUp C SDK in an open-source tool
flags.detail: Access needs developer registration and agreement to Trimble API terms; redistribution terms were not read (forum thread only). Recommended route is export to OBJ/GLB/IFC, Speckle connector, or Rhino 8 import then save .3dm.

flags.claim: Revit .rvt can be converted to IFC or meshes through APS Model Derivative at acceptable cost
flags.detail: The supported-translations table and pricing page are script-rendered and could not be read. Free tier has monthly caps (numbers not retrieved); paid tier uses Flex tokens; per-job price came from a search snippet only.

flags.claim: IFC4X3 geometry imports reliably in web-ifc and IfcOpenShell
flags.detail: web-ifc enumerates IFC4X3 in its schema file, but the IfcOpenShell README (re-read 21 Oct 2026) states extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 TC1 and IFC4 Add2 TC1. Decision in r1: IFC4 ADD2 is the default export and import baseline; IFC4X3 is optional until a tower round-trip spike (IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion, tessellated geometry) passes in IfcOpenShell and web-ifc. Revit's exporter now offers IFC4.3 Reference View requirements, so IFC4.3 input is realistic but unproven.

flags.claim: Speckle object model is stable enough to map Layer 0 to
flags.detail: Speckle 2026.9 replaced the nested object graph with bundles (units per object, no Level object, no proxies); compatibility mode for ACC sync and file uploads ends 1 November 2026, and pre-2026.9 SDKs get a 404 on new versions. r1 retargets the mapping to the 2026.9 model only, pins the 2026.9 SDK and moves Speckle export to v1; the relations page does not describe site or building containers, so the hierarchy mapping is open.

flags.claim: Organiser's 'Site plans & 3D model' download is in a format and CRS the tool can read
flags.detail: The public page does not state formats, CRS, vertical datum or what north arrow it shows (re-checked 21 Oct 2026). Registration closes 29 Oct and Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026. Ask: file formats (.3dm, .skp, .dwg, .ifc?), units, whether the arrow is true, grid or magnetic, vertical datum and Z0, origin, and whether context buildings and approved towers are included. If obtainable, add it as a named CI fixture.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy (1997) is the governing policy for height and view protection
flags.detail: Both policy PDFs named in the brief returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher, as did the City's view-protection pages. I could not determine whether the Higher Buildings Policy Review has superseded or amended the 1997 policy. The view-cones dataset says the City's by-laws are authoritative.

flags.claim: AI-assisted labelling accuracy thresholds (95% auto-accept precision, 80% floor)
flags.detail: No literature on IFC/BIM element classification accuracy was retrieved. These numbers are editable team assumptions to be measured on a labelled VTC test set.

flags.claim: IFC class definitions used in the Layer 0 mapping (IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion semantics)
flags.detail: r1 read the IFC4.3 markdown pages for IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcBuildingStorey, IfcSpatialStructureElement, IfcMapConversion, IfcProjectedCRS, IfcPropertySet, IfcClassificationReference, IfcRoot and Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities from the buildingSMART GitHub docs. Still unconfirmed: the IFC4 ADD2 equivalents (IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion), IfcBuilding composition types for podium plus towers, the direction of IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure, and that mapping massing to IfcSpace is accepted practice. The round-trip spike settles these.

flags.claim: All thresholds with status team_assumption in P14 (completeness, parity, overlap, true-north error 0.25/1 deg, parcel agreement 1/2 m, Z0 agreement 1/3 m, plate-sum error 0.5/2%, memory 50/80% of declared maximum, data age, 100 m tall-building cut-off, floor-to-floor 2.5-6 m, 3-cluster gate, etc.)
flags.detail: Shown in the tool as editable presets with the reasoning in each metric's basis; none has a published source. Where an EPSG accuracy or derived geometry motivates a value, the basis says so.

flags.claim: EPSG:26910 (proj4 +datum=NAD83) is the right CRS for City of Vancouver data, and mixing it with WGS84 shifts positions 2-4 m
flags.detail: City LiDAR 2022 is NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD, not NAD83 original. proj4js defines its nad83 datum with towgs84 0,0,0, so no shift would ever be applied; epsg.io's EPSG:26910 remarks say it is replaced by NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 10N in Canada for accuracy better than 1 m. Evidence: P14-S36, P14-S30, P14-S33, P14-S57.
flags.correction: Project CRS is EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N (towgs84 -0.991,1.9072,0.5129,...), registered in proj4js from the epsg.io string. EPSG lists the CSRS-to-WGS84 transformation accuracy as 1.0 m (alternative 2.0 m); EPSG:26910 stays an accepted import alias with a warning. Parcel-agreement thresholds restated at 1.0 m and 2.0 m.

flags.claim: A local Z = 0 at the entrance floor sidesteps vertical datum mixing
flags.detail: City context heights are geodetic (footprints: baseelev_m and topelev_m 'geodetic'; sample building base 30.7 m, top 219.29 m, height above grade 188.59 m) and LiDAR is CGVD28GVRD; protected-view limits are stated as elevations. A bare local zero cannot be stacked on context or tested against view limits. Evidence: P14-S35, P14-S36, P14-S37.
flags.correction: Z0 geodetic elevation and vertical datum are required georeference fields, defaulted from LiDAR ground at the entrance and confirmed by the user, exported as IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight and IfcProjectedCRS.VerticalDatum. EPSG:3157 itself has no vertical axis (P14-S57).

flags.claim: Speckle keys objects by applicationId (cited to the pre-2026.9 data-schema page)
flags.detail: As cited, wrong: P14-S09 says objects are identified by content hash and applicationId gives stable version tracking, and it covers only versions published before 2026.9. The 2026.9 model pages (P14-S10) key objects by applicationId and do not mention content hashes, so identity depends on the Speckle version.
flags.correction: Store IFC GlobalId, source applicationId, Layer 0 UUID and our own SHA-256 separately; cite P14-S10 for the 2026.9 model and treat P14-S09 as historical.

flags.claim: The meaning of avght_m, maxht_m and the datum of topelev_m in Building footprints 2009 is undocumented
flags.detail: The dataset page documents the fields: baseelev_m and topelev_m are the lowest and highest elevations (geodetic), hgt_agl is essentially topelev minus baseelev, avght_m the average element height, maxht_m and minht_m the max and min over all elements sharing a BLDGID, base_m the base elevation of all elements sharing a BLDGID. Sample building 149845 fits (parts 188.59 m, maxht_m 208.63 m). The page names no vertical datum beyond 'geodetic'.
flags.correction: Field meanings moved to resolved (use maxht_m only for building-level summaries); the name of the vertical datum behind topelev_m stays unresolved.

flags.claim: web-ifc benchmark: 29-70 MB files open in 0.45-1.2 s and mesh in 4.6-7.6 s
flags.detail: This picked a subset. In the same table 47 MB executed in 0.52 s, 55 MB in 2.05 s and 70 MB in 5.5 s while 30 MB took 5.3 s and 34 MB took 7.6 s; open times for 26-70 MB range 0.17-1.16 s. Time does not scale with size, and the M1 listed free RAM of about 137 (units not stated). Evidence: P14-S08.
flags.correction: Quote the full range (open 0.17-1.16 s, execute 0.52-7.6 s for 26-70 MB) and set thresholds from our own measurement of a VTC-sized model on a mid-range Windows laptop.

flags.claim: A 1 degree true-north error moves a shadow tip about 1.7 m, which justifies a 0.5 degree target
flags.detail: The geometry is right but the 100 m shadow was the wrong scale. Derived at latitude 49.29 N: noon altitude at winter solstice = 90 - 49.29 - 23.44 = 17.3 degrees, so a 300 m tower casts about 965 m and 1 degree moves the tip about 17 m; at equinox noon the shadow is about 349 m and the shift about 6 m (244-305 m towers: about 5-6 m equinox, 14-17 m solstice).
flags.correction: Tolerance restated as good <= 0.25 degree, bad >= 1 degree (team assumption that depends on the CLIM packets).

flags.claim: The wasm32 4 GiB memory ceiling is the browser limit for imports
flags.detail: The 4 GiB figure was general knowledge, not an opened page, and as a 'bad' threshold it is unreachable because each module stops at its own declared maximum. Memory64 shipped in Chrome 133, Firefox 134 and Node 24 while Safari has it only in a Technical Preview (P14-S58).
flags.correction: Use each WASM module's declared maximum memory as the limit (good <= 50%, bad >= 80%) and treat Safari as the constraining browser.

flags.claim: Rhino.Compute is not available to Educational licences (in general)
flags.detail: McNeel's page says only that core-hour billing is incompatible with Educational and Commercial licences and that Windows Server cannot take single-computer keys. It does not mention Rhino.Compute or workstation use.
flags.correction: Narrow the claim to what the page says; record workstation licensing as unverified.

flags.claim: Tower height (244-305 m) threshold status is 'verified'
flags.detail: The source P14-S54 is marked opened=false and the metric's own basis said the brief PDF was not opened, so the status contradicted the evidence. The brief's measurement convention is also unknown (CTBUH versus City base surface versus geodetic).
flags.correction: Status corrected; the range is unverified until the brief PDF is read, and the height is shown under three conventions in P14-M05.

flags.claim: Magnetic declination at the Vancouver site is roughly 15 degrees east
flags.detail: Informal general knowledge; no calculation or source was retrieved (NOAA calculator API returned HTTP 400; the NRCan page describes only a manual method). WMM2025 is valid until late 2029, so the tool should compute the value with date and model recorded.

flags.claim: Extrusion and SubD objects in .3dm files can be meshed with rhino3dm
flags.detail: The bindings I read show BrepFace.GetMesh only; bnd_brep.h has no Extrusion or SubD class, bnd_subd binds IsSolid and a few methods but no mesh call, and an Extrusion binding file was not located. Treat extrusions and SubDs as possibly lacking meshes and list them in the import report.

flags.claim: manifold-3d JavaScript exposes slice and volume under the C++ names

notes: Format routes (summary): .3dm = rhino3dm.js/py native (layers, names, ModelUnitSystem, EarthAnchorPoint; B-reps need saved render meshes; extrusion and SubD mesh access unconfirmed). OBJ = native parse, declared unit, no hierarchy or metadata. IFC = web-ifc in browser (IFC2x3 and IFC4 first), IfcOpenShell server-side; IFC4X3 only after the round-trip spike. glTF/GLB = native, metres, Y-up, extras for metadata. FBX = v1. SketchUp .skp = no browser reader; export OBJ/GLB (OBJ needs SketchUp Pro), Speckle connector (SketchUp 2021-2026), or Rhino 8 import then save .3dm. Revit .rvt = IFC export (open-source exporter, LGPLv2, now with IFC4.3 Reference View requirements), Speckle connector (Revit 2023-2027, Windows) or APS Model Derivative (unverified). DWG/DXF = 2D site plans only: Rhino 8 import then save .3dm, or dxf-parser for DXF. Speckle is free for students and educators per its pricing page. CRS and heights: project CRS EPSG:3157 (not 26910); Z0 stored as a geodetic elevation with datum; City data heights are geodetic. Schedule: core is about 17 person-days (team estimate) against about 18 working days to 13 Nov 2026 for two students who also own other packets, so still tight; plan to publish a dated supported-formats list by 28 Oct 2026 (before the 29 Oct registration close), stating only what is implemented that day. Before the organiser Q&A closes on 3 Nov 2026 ask: file formats of the site/3D model, units, which north the arrow shows (true, grid, magnetic), vertical datum and Z0, whether context and approved towers are included. Anonymity: VTC entries are evaluated anonymously and submitted as four image boards, so the anonymised export in P14-M06 covers shared model files and community forks; board file metadata belongs to PRES.
